headline: Ronald Wayne Left Apple Just Days After Its Start

sentences.text: Ronald Wayne helped two young men start Apple.
He drew the first picture for the new business.
He owned a small part of the new company.
He sold his part after 12 days for $800.
He did not want to lose his own money.

grammar.title: Help + Object + Bare Infinitive
grammar.note: The verb 'help' can be followed by an object and a base verb without 'to'. It means assisting someone in performing an action.

grammar.title: Preposition 'For' with Price
grammar.note: The preposition 'for' is used to state the monetary value paid or received for something. Here it shows how much money Wayne received when selling his share.

sentences.text: Ronald Wayne started Apple with Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak in 1976.
He made their first picture sign and wrote basic rules for them.
Ronald owned a 10 percent share, but he worried about company debts.
He feared big money losses because an earlier business failed.
So he sold his share back to them for $800 after 12 days.
People will always remember him as an early partner of the famous company.

grammar.title: Coordinating Conjunction 'But'
grammar.note: The word 'but' connects two complete sentences that show contrasting ideas. It signals a shift from holding equity to feeling anxious.

grammar.title: Adverbial Clause of Reason
grammar.note: The conjunction 'because' introduces a clause explaining the reason behind his fear. The clause contains its own subject and verb.

sentences.text: On April 1, 1976, Ronald Wayne co-founded Apple Computer with Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak.
He received a 10 percent equity, which means ownership in a business, to break tie votes.
Wayne designed the original company logo and wrote the manual for their first computer.
However, he worried about personal liability, which is legal responsibility for corporate financial debts.
Because a past venture had failed, he decided to exit after only 12 days.
Wayne sold his entire share back to his two partners for a total of $800.
He has stated over the years that he does not regret his early decision.

grammar.focus: which means ownership in a business
grammar.title: Non-defining Relative Clause
grammar.note: This clause uses 'which' after a comma to provide extra definition for the term 'equity'. It helps clarify specialized terms without disrupting sentence flow.

grammar.title: Past Perfect Tense
grammar.note: The past perfect 'had failed' shows that the business failure happened prior to another past event ('decided to exit'). It establishes clear temporal sequence.

sentences.text: In April 1976, Ronald Wayne established Apple Computer alongside younger co-founders Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak.
Wayne was granted a 10 percent stake, or partial business ownership, to settle disputes between them.
He created the company's first logo and drafted the official operating manual for the Apple I.
However, when Jobs secured a credit line to buy parts, Wayne feared personal financial exposure.
In a legal partnership, members are personally responsible for corporate debts if the business suffers failure.
Just 12 days after signing the agreement, Wayne formally withdrew his name from the starting firm.
He was paid $800 for relinquishing his equity, followed by an additional $1,500 payout later.
Although that small share eventually became worth billions, Wayne maintained that he made the right choice.

grammar.title: Passive Voice with Ditransitive Verb
grammar.note: When a verb taking two objects ('grant') is made passive, the receiver becomes the subject while the direct object remains behind as a retained object.

grammar.focus: Although that small share eventually became worth billions
grammar.title: Concession Clause with 'Although'
grammar.note: The subordinator 'Although' introduces a contrasting fact that makes the main clause's statement remarkable or unexpected.

sentences.text: When Ronald Wayne co-founded Apple Computer with Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak on April 1, 1976, he assumed the role of seasoned advisor.
The 41-year-old draftsman was allocated a 10 percent equity stake, serving as a neutral tie-breaker during strategic discussions between his younger partners.
Beyond drafting the original partnership contract, Wayne illustrated the firm's initial logo and wrote the operations manual for the Apple I.
However, when Jobs obtained a $15,000 credit line to supply a vendor, Wayne became deeply concerned about potential personal financial liability.
Having spent a year recovering from the traumatic failure of a previous venture, he was reluctant to risk his personal assets.
Consequently, just 12 days after Apple's formation, Wayne officially filed an amendment to relinquish his ownership share in exchange for $800.
He accepted an additional $1,500 payment a year later to forfeit any future financial claims against the newly incorporated technology enterprise.
Decades later, despite missing out on a fortune worth hundreds of billions of dollars, Wayne insisted that he never regretted his decision.

grammar.title: Perfect Participle Clause
grammar.note: The form 'Having + past participle' expresses a completed past background event. It shows why he was reluctant before the main action occurred.

grammar.focus: despite missing out on a fortune
grammar.title: Preposition 'Despite' + Gerund
grammar.note: 'Despite' functions as a preposition and must be followed by a noun phrase or gerund verb form (-ing), rather than a full finite clause.
